# Fixture provenance

These fixtures reproduce the exact output shapes of the two optional tools.
They are derived from upstream sources, not invented.

## llmfit

- Upstream commit: **`53951c3f89aa0dc7afbc0a6d52ccbe27417421e2`**
  (<https://github.com/AlexsJones/llmfit>)
- Read from source, not from prose documentation:
  - `llmfit-tui/src/serve_shared.rs` — `system_json()` and `fit_to_json()`,
    the serializers the CLI actually emits;
  - `llmfit-tui/src/display.rs` — `display_json_system()` and
    `display_json_fits()`, which wrap them in `{ "system": … }` and
    `{ "system": …, "models": [ … ] }`;
  - `llmfit-tui/src/main.rs` — `Commands::Info`, which under `--json` emits
    `display_json_fits(&specs, &[fit])`;
  - `llmfit-core/src/hardware.rs` — `SystemSpecs`, `GpuInfo`, and
    `GpuBackend::label()` (`CUDA`, `Metal`, `ROCm`, `Vulkan`, `SYCL`,
    `CPU (ARM)`, `CPU (x86)`, `NPU (Ascend)`);
  - `llmfit-core/src/fit.rs` — `fit_text()` and `fit_level_code()`. At this
    commit `fit_to_json` emits BOTH: `fit_level` carries the code (`perfect`,
    `good`, `marginal`, `too_tight`) and `fit_label` carries the human string
    (`Perfect`, `Good`, `Marginal`, `Too Tight`). An earlier revision of this
    fixture had the two the wrong way round.
- Retrieved: 2026-08-21.

`llmfit-info.json` is the `llmfit --json info <model>` envelope: one call
returning both `system` and `models`.

Two corrections against the earlier fixture, both found by reading the source:

- **There is no `node` object.** That belongs to the HTTP API
  (`GET /api/v1/system`), not to the CLI. The CLI emits `system` at the top
  level and nothing else beside it.
- **There is no operating-system field anywhere in the CLI output.** ANVILMARK
  therefore observes the OS itself, through an injectable platform observer
  owned by the adapter, and records it as an ANVILMARK deterministic
  observation rather than an llmfit field.

`gpus[]` carries `count` and a per-GPU `backend`; `count` is reconciled against
`gpu_count`, and a contradiction fails closed.

## promptfoo

- Output file format: <https://www.promptfoo.dev/docs/configuration/outputs/>
- Result processing in CI: <https://www.promptfoo.dev/docs/integrations/ci-cd/#processing-results>
- Command-line options: <https://www.promptfoo.dev/docs/usage/command-line/>
- Retrieved: 2026-08-21.
- Shape confirmed by the documented CI snippet
  `const { stats, results: evalResults } = evalOutput.results;`, and by the
  documented envelope carrying `version`, `timestamp`, and
  `results.{prompts,stats}`.
- Upstream commit: **`0170037970dd4732f7542c60ceafa5f4951289de`**
  (<https://github.com/promptfoo/promptfoo>), read from source rather than
  prose:
  - `src/types/index.ts` — `OutputFile` (`evalId`, `results`, `config`,
    `shareableUrl`), `EvaluateSummaryV3` (`version: 3`, `timestamp`,
    `results[]`, `prompts[]`, `stats`), and `EvaluateStats` (`successes`,
    `failures`, `errors`, `tokenUsage`);
  - `src/util/output.ts` — the JSON branch, which writes
    `JSON.stringify(outputData, null, 2)` to the `-o` path.
- `version` and `timestamp` live INSIDE `results` in both V2 and V3. The
  earlier `promptfoo-eval-output-flat.json` fixture placed them at the top
  level, which no current version emits; it has been removed rather than
  parsed, since supporting a shape the tool does not produce is not
  compatibility.
- `EvaluateResult.provider` is `Pick<ProviderOptions, "id" | "label">` — an
  object — while `CompletedPromptSchema.provider` is a plain string. Both are
  read.
- Files:
  - `promptfoo-eval-output.json` — **generated by running promptfoo 0.122.0**
    against the config ANVILMARK generates for the default one-row, one-prompt
    test spec, using the built-in `echo` provider. One case, one success.
  - `promptfoo-eval-output-two-cases.json` — the same, for a two-row spec whose
    second assertion fails. Two cases, one success, one failure.
  - `promptfoo-eval-output-multi-provider.json` — hand-built: the same envelope
    naming two providers, which must be refused. It is not a real artifact
    because promptfoo will not produce one for a spec this adapter can express,
    which permits exactly one provider. It is refused at attribution, before
    any count is examined.

  - `promptfoo-eval-output-error-row.json` — **generated by running promptfoo
    0.122.0** with its `http` provider against a closed port on `127.0.0.1`.
    Nothing left the machine. One case, `success: false, failureReason: 2`, and
    the summary counts one error. promptfoo attributes the row to the URL
    `http://127.0.0.1:9/` rather than to the id `http`, so this artifact can
    never be attributed by the adapter; it exists to check the per-case rule on a
    genuine error row.

**Exported, not sent.** Every fixture is promptfoo's EXPORTED form. The
0.122.0 exporter rewrites JSON-valued strings compactly and replaces strings it
judges to be secrets (`src/util/sanitizer.ts:750-775`), so a fixture's
`vars`, assertion values and prompt text are what promptfoo wrote, which is not
always byte-for-byte what it sent. None of the committed fixtures contains a
string the exporter changes. Synthetic artifacts for row-binding tests are built
by `test/promptfoo-artifacts.ts` in the same row shape.

**Normalisation.** Generated artifacts embed local machine paths: the output
path under the per-user temporary directory, and stack frames inside the error
row's message. Every such absolute path is replaced with `<local-path>`. That is
the ONLY change: the summary stats and every row's `success` and
`failureReason` were asserted unchanged by the normalising script, and the
adapter reads neither `config.outputPath` nor the `error` string. The first two
fixtures were committed in `37f26ff` before this normalisation, so that commit
still contains a per-user temporary-directory path; it is not a credential, but
it is machine identity, and `test/trust-boundary.test.ts` now fails if any
fixture contains an absolute local path.

The first two were previously hand-written and reported 38 successes and 2
failures for a spec with ONE case. That mismatch was recorded as available T3
evidence, so they are now generated from the real tool and their counts
reconcile with the spec they stand for. Regenerate with a run of
`promptfoo eval -c <generated config> -o <fixture>` against 0.122.0.

Provider identity is read from every documented location — `results.prompts[]`,
`results.results[]`, and `results.providers[]` — and reconciled. Disagreement,
absence, or more than one provider is refused rather than aggregated.
